title: Pulled-back atlas and common-refinement test for local quasi-finiteness
statement: Let $S,T,B,U$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $T,B,U$ over $S$, let $b:B\to T$ be an $S$-morphism, let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to h_T$ be a morphism. Write $h_Z(H)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(H,Z)$. Suppose $a:h_U\to X$ is representable surjective etale. Form $X_B=X\times_{h_T}h_B$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and $U_B=U\times_TB$ [def-pc-fibre-product], using the scheme map $U\to T$ induced by $fa$. There is a canonical identification $h_{U_B}\cong h_U\times_X X_B$, compatible with both projections. The induced $a_B:h_{U_B}\to X_B$ is representable surjective etale, and for every scheme $D\to X_B$ there is a canonical isomorphism $h_D\times_{X_B}h_{U_B}\cong h_D\times_Xh_U$ over $h_D$. For every representable etale chart $v:h_V\to X_B$, the sheaf $h_V\times_{X_B}h_{U_B}$ is represented by a scheme $W$; its projections $p:W\to V$ and $q:W\to U_B$ are respectively surjective etale and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and their composites to $B$ agree. If $U_B\to B$ is locally quasi-finite in the scheme sense [pqf-def-quasifinite], then both $W\to B$ and $V\to B$ are locally quasi-finite. No separatedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0ABM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus), atlas diagram in the proof; Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), common-refinement proof; Tag 03XJ (definition-locally-quasi-finite). Source-locality input: descent.tex Tag 03X4 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-etale-local-source).

proof.text: Regard $h_T,h_B$ as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] to $X\to h_T\leftarrow h_B$ to obtain the algebraic space $X_B$ with its projections. By full faithfulness in [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], $fa:h_U\to h_T$ is induced by a unique $S$-scheme map $c:U\to T$. Form $U_B=U\times_T B$ using [def-pc-fibre-product].

For every $S$-scheme $H$, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $h_{U_B}(H)$ with pairs $(u,\beta)$ satisfying $c u=b\beta$. Send such a pair to $(u,(a(u),\beta))$ in $(h_U\times_X X_B)(H)$. Its inverse sends $(u,(x,\beta))$ with $a(u)=x$ to $(u,\beta)$. These are inverse because $x=a(u)$, and commute with restriction along every $H\prime\to H$ because restriction is precomposition. They therefore define the claimed sheaf isomorphism. Both projections have the asserted values; in particular $a_B(u,\beta)=(a(u),\beta)$.

source.place: Tag 0ABM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite-locus), proof, pulled-back atlas diagram; explicit fibre-product universal-property calculation.

proof.text: Fix $t:h_D\to X_B$ and write its components as $t_X:h_D\to X$ and $\beta_D:h_D\to h_B$. On $H$-sections, send $(d,(u,\beta))$ in $h_D\times_{X_B}h_{U_B}$ to $(d,u)$. The defining equations are exactly $a(u)=t_X(d)$ and $\beta=\beta_D(d)$; hence the inverse sends $(d,u)$ to $(d,(u,\beta_D(d)))$. The compatibility with $T$ follows from $f t_X=b\beta_D$. These formulas are natural and preserve the projection to $h_D$, proving the second canonical isomorphism. By the scheme-test definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space], $h_D\times_X h_U$ is represented by a scheme $E$ and its projection $E\to D$ is surjective etale, since $a$ is representable surjective etale. The displayed identification makes the test of $a_B$ this very projection. This holds for every $D,t$, so $a_B$ is representable surjective etale.

source.place: Tag 025V (definition-relative-representable-property); Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space), scheme-test meaning of representable surjective etale.

proof.text: For $v:h_V\to X_B$, apply the scheme-test definition [def-trf-algebraic-space] to $a_B$ at $h_V$ to obtain a representing scheme $W$ and a surjective etale projection $p:W\to V$. The same fibre product with its factors interchanged is the scheme test of the representable etale map $v$ at $h_{U_B}$, so its other projection $q:W\to U_B$ is etale. On sections its defining equality is $v(z)=a_B(u,\beta)$; projecting to $h_B$ says that the two composites to $B$ agree. Full faithfulness [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] turns this equality of natural transformations into equality of scheme morphisms. Write $g:V\to B$ and $r:U_B\to B$ for these maps; then $gp=rq$.

source.place: Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), proof, common-refinement diagram; spaces.tex Tag 025V and categories.tex Tag 001P.

proof.text: Assume $r:U_B\to B$ is locally quasi-finite. Apply the forward implication of [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-etale-source-locality] to the etale map $q:W\to U_B$ and $r$; it gives that $rq:W\to B$ is locally quasi-finite. Since $gp=rq$, apply the converse of that same node to the surjective etale map $p:W\to V$ and $g:V\to B$ to conclude that $g$ is locally quasi-finite. Both applications concern schemes and have precisely the stated hypotheses. No separatedness or quasi-compactness is used.
